title_en: Ingent holds Oracle transformation strategy webinar... “Reduce costs and risks through customized migration”
summary_en: [ZD Net Korea] Ingent introduced a customized migration strategy for companies that want to reduce their dependence on Oracle database (DB) and switch to an open source-based environment. Ingent announced on the 27th that it held a webinar with the theme of 'Leaving Oracle, a customized migration strategy to realize customer value.' At this event, corporate officials who are considering reducing Oracle DB operating costs and eliminating vendor dependency attended and showed great interest. The webinar introduced the background of PostgreSQL emerging as a major alternative along with the recent trend of companies switching to open source databases. Ingent explained that the adoption of PostgreSQL is increasing in various industries such as finance, public sector, and distribution due to the burden of license costs and dependency on specific vendors. Ingent presented an approach by dividing the database conversion process into two areas: data transfer and application conversion. In the case of data migration, it was revealed that stability can be secured by using a conversion tool that has been proven in multiple projects. Regarding application conversion, two strategies were introduced: automation and minimal change. title_en: Go Sam-seok, former member of the Korea Communications Commission, appointed as broadcasting, communications, and culture advisor directly to the Speaker of the National Assembly
summary_en: [ZD Net Korea] Speaker of the National Assembly Cho Jeong-sik appointed Professor Ko Sam-seok of Dongguk University as a direct advisor to the Speaker of the National Assembly to advise on policies in the fields of broadcasting, communications, and culture. title_ja: ソウル大-アイサイコリア、「SAR衛星データなど共同研究」

title_en: Korea Post issues 420,000 commemorative stamps for ‘Yeosu World Island Expo’
summary_en: [ZD Net Korea] In commemoration of this year's 'Yeosu World Island Expo', 420,000 commemorative stamps containing the symbol of Yeosu will be issued on the 4th of next month. The Korea Post announced on the 27th that it will issue 420,000 commemorative stamps for the 'Yeosu World Island Expo' to commemorate the international expo held under the theme of 'islands'. The stamps will be issued on September 4th. The expo aims to 'connect islands, the sea and the future' Under the slogan, it will be held from September 5 to November 4 in the Jinmo district of Dolsan, Yeosu-si, Jeollanam-do, the Yeosu World Island Expo Center, and the area around Geumo-do and Gaedo. The commemorative stamp contains symbols of Yeosu, such as a bridge, a marine cable car, a lighthouse, and camellia flowers, against the backdrop of the sunset-colored scenery of Yeosu. Park In-hwan, head of the Korea Post, said, “The purpose of publicizing the charm of the island and Yeosu through the issuance of a commemorative stamp is to spread the word.” Of course, I hope it will be an opportunity to reflect on the precious value of the island,” he said.

title_en: Bill Gates warns of “AI turbulence”… Proposes ‘human-only jobs’ and ‘token tax’
summary_en: Bill Gates, founder of Microsoft (MS), urged governments around the world to take preemptive responses, saying the rapid development of AI could lead to the most turbulent period in human history. It is a warning that AI can replace jobs on a large scale, enhance cyber attacks and biological threats, and also affect human relationships and the growth of children. In particular, he proposed designating some jobs as ‘Human Reserved’ areas and imposing taxes on AI tokens and robots. In an essay published on the 26th (local time), founder Gates said, “AI is going through one of the most turbulent periods in human history.”
